# Agatha Sowerby

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Role:** Homemaker and community organizer  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Agatha Sowerby is a stout, heavy woman who walks with a waddle. She has a heavy and awkward frame, weighing around two hundred pounds. She maintains a vigilant, perceptive gaze from her kitchen window.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c9 P16](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0016), [v1 c9 P31](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0031), [v1 c23 P30](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0030)_

## Personality

Agatha Sowerby is a proficient, highly inquisitive homemaker who pays vigilant attention to her neighbors' affairs. She prides herself on always expressing her mind freely, without dread or partiality, though her blunt remarks about others' appearances can hurt their feelings. She enjoys causing a stir and sharing information throughout the community. Despite her intrusive and candid nature, she possesses a kindly heart and is quick to forgive genuine apologies.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c1 P30](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0030), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c9 P45](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0045), [v1 c10 P1](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0001), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c10 P38](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0038), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Agatha Sowerby lived in a home situated at Sowerby's Hollow in Brierley, sitting by her window to watch everyone passing along the main road. One June afternoon, she spotted Obed Abernethy driving out of Brierley dressed in fine clothes, which ruined her peace until she visited Grey Shutters to learn from Thirza that Obed had gone to collect an orphan boy. Upon learning the next day that a red-haired orphan girl, Nell Harcourt, arrived instead due to a mix-up, Mrs. Agatha expressed strong disapproval. Weeks later, after recovering from a bout of influenza, Mrs. Agatha visited Grey Shutters to inspect Nell and made blunt remarks calling her plain, thin, freckled, and red-headed, provoking Nell into a fiery rage. When Nell later visited her home to deliver a dramatic, remorseful apology, Mrs. Agatha readily forgave her, offered her hope about her hair, and gave her white June lilies. Over the following years, Mrs. Agatha remained an active presence in Brierley, participating in political rallies, Aid Society meetings, and community events. She eventually admitted she was wrong in her initial harsh assessment of Nell, acknowledging that the girl had grown into an attractive and clever young lady.
